subject: Banking
title: The Goldsmiths Who Created Money
description: One-minute skill: The Goldsmiths Who Created Money.

hook.text: London goldsmiths in the 1600s discovered they could lend out deposited gold because not everyone withdraws at once.

buildup.text: Customers received paper receipts for their gold. These receipts circulated as money. Nobody came for the actual gold.

discovery.text: Goldsmiths issued more receipts than gold they held. They created money from nothing.

twist.text: It worked until too many people asked for their gold at once. The first bank runs were goldsmith runs.

climax.text: Goldsmiths accidentally invented modern banking. Lend more than you have and hope nobody asks for it all back.

punchline.text: More receipts than gold. Goldsmiths invented fractional reserve banking.

quiz.question: What did London goldsmiths accidentally invent?

details.summary: London goldsmiths in the 17th century accidentally invented fractional reserve banking when they realized they could lend out deposited gold since not all depositors would demand it back simultaneously, creating money through lending.
details.whyItMatters: Goldsmith banking is the origin of how all modern banks work. The discovery that banks could lend more than they held in reserve created the money multiplier effect that funds the majority of economic activity today.
takeaways: Goldsmiths issued receipts for stored gold that circulated as the first banknotes
They discovered most depositors never returned for their gold simultaneously
Lending out deposited gold created more money in circulation than gold existed

faq.question: How did goldsmiths accidentally create banking?
faq.answer: Customers deposited gold for safekeeping and received paper receipts. The receipts began circulating as payment since they were easier to carry than gold. Goldsmiths realized they could issue more receipts than gold held, creating new money.

faq.question: Was goldsmith banking risky?
faq.answer: Extremely. If too many depositors demanded their gold at once, the goldsmith could not pay all of them because some gold had been lent out. This fundamental vulnerability is the same bank run risk that exists in every fractional reserve bank today.
